output.summary: An herb native to Southeast Asia, small water-pepper has creeping, slender stems, narrow tapering leaves and minute pale-violet flowers. In Malaysia and Indonesia, its shoots and young leaves are eaten raw in salads, used to flavour peppery dishes, or made into tea.
